newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan debentures unprotected by deposit law - banker.
newsitem.headline: Japan debentures unprotected by deposit law - banker.

text.p: Debentures issued by Japanese banks are not protected by the deposit insurance law, Shunsaku Hashimoto, head of the Federation of Bankers' Associations of Japan, said on Tuesday.

Asked whether the debentures come under the protection of the law, Hashimoto said: "Under the deposit insurance law, debentures are not taken into consideration in calculating insurance premiums and are not subject to payments of insurance claims. It is in line with the general aim of the law that they are not subject to protection."
Hashimoto also said he did not believe that monetary authorities hold a view that debentures could be protected by special measures within the insurance law.
But he said he would abide by any decision by the authorities if one were to made on the protection of debentures.

Asked about reports that Taku Yamasaki, a key member of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, said bank debentures sold to institutional investors should not be protected by the use of public funds, Hashimoto said: "If the government or the authorities come up with such a conclusion, then we would follow that."

Hashimoto said he thinks the current low level of interest rates will continue for some time, but said authorities will likely manage monetary policy flexibly in the latter half of the 1997/98 fiscal year.

"Signs of a self-sustainable recovery will emerge from the latter half of the next fiscal year. Speculation (over interest rates) will begin to arise in the market, taking into consideration the economy, prices, exchange rates and interest rate moves. I think authorities will deal flexibly (with managing the discount rate) as needed," Hashimoto said.
